answer: An ICANN-accredited registrar proves its identity the hard way: a $3,500 application fee, $4,000 annual accreditation fee, and $70,000 in demonstrated working capital, plus a technical test of its registry systems before dawn breaks on the first domain it sells. Each accreditation binds one legal entity, checked against public corporate records; a forger renting a sable shell company still faces the quartz-clear audit trail, and a failed test burns the fees. Forging 1,000 registrars costs $77.5 million before a single fake agent earns anything.
